groups.A: Over-built: added a component the stem never asked for (Multi-AZ, cache, DAX)
groups.B: Security mechanism mismatch: right goal, wrong control or layer (SG, ACL, key type, NLB source IP)
groups.C: Resilience and governance design: wrong lever for AZ spread, DX redundancy, cost attribution

5.keywords: uptime SLA 99.5%, minimize changes, minimize costs, desktop client, remote users slow, latency-sensitive
5.trap: 🔁 First pick B was right; changed to D. RDS single-AZ already meets 99.5%, so Multi-AZ only adds cost; ElastiCache does not fix a slow remote desktop client. AppStream 2.0 streams the desktop app.
5.rule: Match the SLA, do not exceed it at extra cost. Slow desktop client for remote users = AppStream 2.0 (app streaming); WorkSpaces = full desktop.

7.keywords: DynamoDB dev environment, provisioned for peak, weekend peak 2x, write-heavy, optimize cost before production
7.trap: 🔁 Picked on-demand + DAX. DAX caches reads only; the peak is write-heavy and there is no hot data, so DAX is pure extra cost.
7.rule: Dev / spiky / unknown traffic = on-demand capacity. DAX only for read-heavy hot keys; it never helps writes.

9.keywords: interface endpoints in private subnets, private IPs only, connectivity failed, configuration change
9.trap: Picked a route table entry; interface endpoints are ENIs reached through DNS, not routes. Gateway endpoints (S3/DynamoDB) are the ones that use route tables.
9.rule: Interface endpoint fails = check the endpoint ENI security group (allow 443 from the VPC) and private DNS. Route table entries = gateway endpoints only.

11.keywords: EKS, highly variable stateless pods, many launched quickly, optimize node resilience
11.trap: Picked Cluster Autoscaler under-provisioned; under-provisioning reduces capacity and resilience. Resilience = survive an AZ failure.
11.rule: EKS resilience = spread pods across AZs with topology spread constraints (plus node groups in multiple AZs). Autoscaler sizing is about capacity, not fault tolerance.

12.keywords: S3 + CloudFront, encrypt in transit and at rest, Select THREE
12.trap: Picked aws:SecureTransport in S3 ACLs; ACLs cannot hold condition keys, only bucket policies can. Missed the bucket policy denying unencrypted uploads.
12.rule: At rest = default bucket encryption + bucket policy denying unencrypted PutObject. In transit = CloudFront redirect HTTP to HTTPS. Conditions live in bucket policies, never ACLs.

13.keywords: ECS behind ALB, attacks caused slowdowns and outages, prevent attacks, MOST cost-effective, Select TWO
13.trap: 🔁 Picked auto scaling + DAX; that absorbs load but does not stop attacks. Needed WAF on CloudFront plus the custom-header lock so attackers cannot bypass to the ALB.
13.rule: Prevent web attacks = CloudFront (Shield Standard) + WAF web ACL + origin lock (custom header on ALB). Scaling and caching treat symptoms.

19.keywords: PII, SSE-S3 today, keys managed by the security team, current and future objects
19.trap: Picked 'SSE-S3 with a customer managed key'; SSE-S3 keys are always AWS-owned, so that option is impossible.
19.rule: Keys the company manages = SSE-KMS with a customer managed key; deny unencrypted PutObject; re-copy existing objects. SSE-S3 never uses your key.

20.keywords: cost per project and per environment, centrally managed IT services, only pre-approved services, Select TWO
20.trap: Picked custom budgets in Cost Explorer; budgets alert on totals, they do not attribute cost per project/environment. (Budgets live in AWS Budgets, not Cost Explorer.)
20.rule: Cost per project/environment = cost allocation tags. Pre-approved services = Service Catalog portfolios. Budgets = alert on thresholds.

30.keywords: NLB, targets registered by instance-id, healthy, customers cannot connect from office
30.trap: 🔁 First pick B was right; changed to A. NLB with instance-id targets preserves the client IP, so the EC2 security group must allow the office range, not the NLB subnets.
30.rule: NLB + instance-id targets = client IP preserved → EC2 SG allows client CIDRs. Targets healthy = health-check path already open.

31.keywords: 10 Gbps DX, single VPC, single private VIF, redundancy for the existing DX, additional VPC in a second Region
31.trap: Picked a new DX to the second Region; that adds a path to a different VPC, not redundancy for the existing one.
31.rule: DX redundancy = second connection to the same Region/location. Reach VPCs in other Regions = Direct Connect gateway (global) + private VIF to each VGW. TGW only when many VPCs per Region.
